lines.japanese: 「いや、おれは山科さんと組むよ」
lines.english: “No. I'll pair up with Yamashina.”

lines.japanese: 付きあってるからって、いつでもどこでも二人セットみたいに考えられるのは、ちょっと恥ずかしい。渡来さんにしても、そう思うところはあるはずだ。
lines.english: It was a little embarrassing to have people assume that dating meant we had to be joined at the hip everywhere we went. Watarai must have felt the same way to some extent.

lines.japanese: それに、山科さんとも久しぶりに『鷹は舞いおりた』やＲ‐ウィング関連の話をしてみたいと思っていた。
lines.english: Besides, it had been a long time since Yamashina and I talked about *The Hawk Has Landed* or anything related to R-Wing.
“Me?”

lines.japanese: 「うん。どうかな」
lines.english: “Yes. What do you say?”

lines.japanese: 僕は山科さんに訊ねた。
lines.english: I asked Yamashina.

lines.japanese: 「どう……なの？」
lines.english: “What... do you say?”

lines.japanese: 山科さんは渡来さんに訊ねた。
lines.english: Yamashina asked Watarai.

lines.japanese: 「なんで？　いんじゃない？　ねえ？」
lines.english: “Why ask me? It's fine, isn't it? Right?”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんは針生さんに訊ねた。
lines.english: Watarai asked Kuroudo.

lines.japanese: 「クク、たまんねえな、この空気。渇くよなァ？」
lines.english: “Kukuku. I can't get enough of this atmosphere. Makes you thirsty, doesn't it?”

lines.japanese: 針生さんは僕に訊ねた。
lines.english: Kuroudo asked me.

lines.japanese: けれど質問の意図がさっぱり分からないので、曖昧に首をひねることしか出来なかった。
lines.english: But I had no idea what his question meant, so all I could do was tilt my head noncommittally.

lines.japanese: 「そしたら、おれたちはＤ列から始めるね。行こう、山科さん」
lines.english: “Then we'll start at Row D. Come on, Yamashina.”

lines.japanese: 「うん。じゃあ、ちょっと借りるね」
lines.english: “Okay. I'll borrow him for a while, then.”

lines.japanese: 僕は配置図を広げながら担当区域へ向かった。山科さんは渡来さんに軽く会釈していた。
lines.english: I unfolded the floor plan and headed for our assigned area. Yamashina gave Watarai a small bow.

lines.japanese: 「先輩、学習能力のない男って一生そのままなのかな。昨日けっこー言ったんだけど」
lines.english: “Kuroudo, do men who never learn stay that way their whole lives? I gave him a pretty thorough talking-to yesterday.”

lines.japanese: 「ククク、おもしれえ。いっそあのロンリーガール、羽田と間違いでも起こさねえかなァ、クハハ」
lines.english: “Kukuku. This is good. Maybe that lonely girl will go and make some mistake with Haneda. Kahaha.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんと針生さんは、さっそく何事か語りあっていたようだ。やっぱり旧知の仲、なんだかんだ言って仲がいいんだ。
lines.english: Watarai and Kuroudo immediately seemed to start talking about something. They really were old friends. Whatever they said, they got along well.

lines.japanese: 「えっ？　それじゃ山科さんの詩を、ロックバードが歌ったことあるの？」
lines.english: “What? Rockbird performed one of your poems?”

lines.japanese: 「うん。ライブの中で余興っぽくだけどね」
lines.english: “Yes. Just for fun, during a concert.”

lines.japanese: 「ＭＣで『鷹おり』の話になったとき、ドラムのひとが『瑠樺ってやつのポエムはなかなかロックだ』とか言いだして。即興で」
lines.english: “They started talking about *Hawk Has Landed* to the crowd, and the drummer said, ‘That Ruka girl’s poetry is pretty rockin’.’ Then they improvised something.”

lines.japanese: 「すごいじゃない！」
lines.english: “That's amazing!”

lines.japanese: 「そうだね、嬉しかったけど、欲をいえばＫｕＲｉＹａに歌ってほしかったかな」
lines.english: “It made me happy. Though if I'm being greedy, I would have liked KuRiYa to sing it.”

lines.japanese: 「はは……山科さん、ドラムのひと嫌いだもんね……」
lines.english: “Haha... You really don't like the drummer, do you?”

lines.japanese: 「嫌いってわけじゃないよ。ただ、ロクバの中では、ひとり違う方角を向きすぎてるかなって」
lines.english: “I don't dislike him. He just seems to face a completely different direction from everyone else in Rockbird.”

lines.japanese: 山科さんはロックバードのドラムス“ハリュー”の正体が、針生蔵人そのひとであることを知らない。
lines.english: Yamashina didn't know that Rockbird's drummer, Haryuu, was none other than Kuroudo Hariu.

lines.japanese: 少なくとも、知らないということになっている。
lines.english: At least, officially she didn't.

lines.japanese: けれど洞察力に優れた山科さんのことだ。たぶん本当は、とっくに気付いているんだろう。
lines.english: But Yamashina was extremely perceptive. In truth, she had probably noticed long ago.

lines.japanese: 誰よりも空気の読める山科さんは、表現者とフォロワーが近付きすぎるべきではない、というハリュー・クロードの意思を汲んで、あくまで学園生活においては一同級生を貫いているのだと思う。
lines.english: Better than anyone at reading a room, she understood Claude Haryuu's desire to keep performer and follower from growing too close. I thought that was why, at school, she always treated him strictly as an ordinary classmate.

lines.japanese: 「そうかあ、瑠樺君の詩はおれもすごいと思ってたんだよなあ。やっぱり本当にすごかったんだあ」
lines.english: “I see. I always thought Ruka's poems were amazing too. So they truly were amazing.”

lines.japanese: 「うーん、自分の好きなものが実力あるひとに認められるって、なんか嬉しいなあ。あ、おれが喜ぶことじゃないか、はは」
lines.english: “It feels wonderful when someone talented recognizes something you love. Oh, I’m not the one who should be celebrating, am I? Haha.”

lines.japanese: 「……あれ、山科さん？　どうしたの」
lines.english: “...Yamashina? Is something wrong?”

lines.japanese: 「……ほんとに？」
lines.english: “...Do you really mean that?”

lines.japanese: 「え、なにが？」
lines.english: “Mean what?”

lines.japanese: 「ドラムのひとはちょっと感性が普通じゃないから、偶然ハマっちゃったみたいだけど、実際私の創作物ってそれほど大したものではないんじゃないかな」
lines.english: “The drummer has somewhat abnormal sensibilities, so my work happened to strike a chord with him. But perhaps the things I create aren't actually very good.”

lines.japanese: 「そんなことないよ。おれ『鷹おり』でもレス付けたことあるでしょ、本当にこう……上手く言えないけど、すごいなって思ったもん」
lines.english: “That's not true. You saw me leave comments on *Hawk Has Landed*, didn't you? I really... I can't put it well, but I truly thought it was amazing.”

lines.japanese: 「ありがとう。誉められることに慣れてなくて、最初から疑って掛かっちゃうのは私の悪い癖だね。でも、社交辞令だと思った方が楽な局面ってあるでしょ？」
lines.english: “Thank you. I’m not used to praise, so I tend to doubt it before anything else. Bad habit of mine. But sometimes it’s easier to assume people are just being polite, isn’t it?”

lines.japanese: 「社交辞令じゃないよ。おれ本当に、ああいうの大好き」
lines.english: “I'm not just being polite. I really love things like that.”

lines.japanese: 「ありがとう。でも、面と向かって好きなんて言われると、照れる」
lines.english: “Thank you. But when you tell me to my face that you love it, I get embarrassed.”

lines.japanese: 「え……あ、いや……うん、ごめん」
lines.english: “Oh... Uh... Right. Sorry.”

lines.japanese: 「ふふ。いいなあ、こういう穏やかな高揚感。シンプルに幸せを享受できる子供のころに戻ったみたい」
lines.english: “Hehe. This gentle excitement is nice. It feels as if I've gone back to childhood, when I could simply accept happiness.”

lines.japanese: 「大人になるうち、対人関係の中で感覚を共有できる機会ってどんどん減ってきちゃったよね」
lines.english: “As we grow up, we get fewer and fewer chances to share the same feelings with another person.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、うん、そうかも……」
lines.english: “Oh. Yes, maybe...”

lines.japanese: 「でも……うーん、交友の発展って、必ずしも幸福な面ばかりじゃないかもなあ」
lines.english: “But... Hmm. A friendship growing deeper may not bring happiness in every respect.”

lines.japanese: 「え、なにそれ。なんか、仲良くなるのは悪いことって言ってるみたい」
lines.english: “What does that mean? You make it sound like becoming close is a bad thing.”

lines.japanese: 「鈍いなあ。それが羽田君のいいところだけど」
lines.english: “You really are dense. Though that's one of your good qualities.”

lines.japanese: 「ええ、おれ鈍い？　ううん、やっぱりそうかあ。いろんなひとに言われちゃうから、最近は気を付けてるんだけどなあ」
lines.english: “What? I'm dense? Hmm. I suppose I must be. So many people tell me that. I've been trying to watch out for it lately.”

lines.japanese: 「そのぐらいで丁度いいと思うよ。鋭くて先回りしちゃうような羽田君だったら、私はちょっと困るかも」
lines.english: “I think you're just right the way you are. I might be in trouble if you were sharp enough to see things coming.”

lines.japanese: そう言って山科さんは、はにかむように微笑んだ。
lines.english: With that, Yamashina smiled bashfully.

lines.japanese: なんだか、からかわれてみたいで、僕は咳ばらいをして恥ずかしさをごまかした。
lines.english: I felt as though she were teasing me, so I cleared my throat to hide my embarrassment.

lines.japanese: 「んッ、んんッ……はあ、周り紙に囲まれてるからかな、ちょっと喉渇いちゃった」
lines.english: “Ahem... Maybe it's because we're surrounded by paper, but my throat is a little dry.”

lines.japanese: 「紙は関係ないと思うよ」
lines.english: “I don't think the paper has anything to do with it.”

lines.japanese: 「んっと、外に自販機あったよね。お茶買ってこようかな。山科さん、なにか要る？」
lines.english: “There was a vending machine outside, wasn't there? Maybe I'll go buy some tea. Would you like anything, Yamashina?”

lines.japanese: 「羽田君、潔癖症なひとだったっけ？」
lines.english: “Were you always a germaphobe, Haneda?”

lines.japanese: 「おれ？　さあ、そんなことないと思うけど」
lines.english: “Me? No. I don't think so.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ、これどうぞ」
lines.english: “Then here.”

lines.japanese: 差しだされたのは、ステンレス製の小ぶりな円筒。
lines.english: She held out a small stainless-steel cylinder.

lines.japanese: 「携帯マグ……山科さんの？」
lines.english: “A travel mug... Is this yours?”

lines.japanese: 「中はただの水だけどね。私、薬が多いから、昔から持ちあるいてるの。元祖水筒女子だよね」
lines.english: “It's only water inside. I've taken a lot of medicine since I was young, so I've always carried it with me. I suppose that makes me the original water-bottle girl.”

lines.japanese: 「どうも……」
lines.english: “Thank you...”

lines.japanese: 遠慮がちに受けとる。ワンタッチで蓋を開けたら、そこはもう飲み口だ。
lines.english: I accepted it hesitantly. One press opened the lid, and there was the mouthpiece.

lines.japanese: いいのだろうか。
lines.english: Was this really all right?

lines.japanese: これに口を付けるのは、叔父さんの箸や森里君のペットボトルを拝借するのと微妙に違うニュアンスな気がする。
lines.english: Putting my mouth to this somehow felt different from borrowing my uncle's chopsticks or Morisato's plastic bottle.

lines.japanese: 意識するわけではないけれど、エチケットとして他の容器に移してから戴くべきだろうか。意識するわけではないけれど、最近は風邪も流行っている。意識するわけではないけれど、山科さんの唇はとても柔らかそ──
lines.english: Not that I was conscious of it, but perhaps etiquette demanded that I pour the water into another container first. Not that I was conscious of it, but colds had been going around lately. Not that I was conscious of it, but Yamashina's lips looked so soft—

lines.japanese: 「小学生か」
lines.english: “Are you in grade school?”

lines.japanese: 「うわあっ」
lines.english: “Waaah!”

lines.japanese: 気付いたら渡来さんと針生さんが後ろに立っていた。
lines.english: Before I knew it, Watarai and Kuroudo were standing behind me.

lines.japanese: 「ど、どうしたの、渡来さんたちはＡ列の棚じゃなかったっけ」
lines.english: “What are you two doing here? Weren't your shelves in Row A?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、ちょっと気分転換に君らの様子見に来たんだけど、まずかった？」
lines.english: “Yes. We came to see how you were doing for a change of pace. Is that a problem?”

lines.japanese: 「ま、まずいなんて、まさかそんなわけ……ねえ、山科さん」
lines.english: “A-a problem? Of course not... Right, Yamashina?”

lines.japanese: 「うーん、どうかな」
lines.english: “Hmm. I wonder.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、あはは……やめようよ、そんな冗談……」
lines.english: “Ahaha... Come on, stop joking like that...”

lines.japanese: 言葉に詰まってますます喉が渇いた僕は、針生さんのミネラルウォーターを分けてもらった。
lines.english: My words caught in my throat, leaving me thirstier than ever, so I had Kuroudo share some of his mineral water with me.

lines.japanese: こうして羽田班の一日バイトは終わった。
lines.english: And so the Haneda team's day at the bookstore came to an end.
